title: Inner-ear CT · Dataset A specimen 1

space.name: Dataset A specimen 1, original temporal-bone CT grid
space.correspondence: Paired Dataset A original arrays have identical IJK dimensions. The source attaches the shared NRRD-style physical grid to raw/raw-0; label/label-0 has no independent grid. Only the explicit LPS-to-RAS coordinate basis is converted. There is no registration to another specimen or atlas.

ct.unit_basis: The source publication reports a reconstructed isotropic 98.6 micrometer grid; the original space-direction magnitudes are 0.0986328125 mm.

image_evidence.calibration: The publication describes HU reconstruction; this HDF5 image has no explicit intensity-unit or calibration attributes. No calibration is inferred or applied.
image_evidence.acquisition: Dataset A cadaveric temporal bone; cone-beam CT reconstruction. Reported acquired slice thickness: 0.466 mm.
image_evidence.sampling: The source publication reports a reconstructed isotropic 98.6 micrometer grid; the original space-direction magnitudes are 0.0986328125 mm. Reconstruction spacing is not acquired spatial resolution.

sources.title: Human Inner Ear Anatomy: Labeled Volume CT Data of Inner Ear Fluid Space and Anatomical Landmarks
sources.citation: Stebani J, Blaimer M, Neun T, Pelt DM, Rak K. Human Inner Ear Anatomy: Labeled Volume CT Data of Inner Ear Fluid Space and Anatomical Landmarks. Zenodo (2023), doi:10.5281/zenodo.8277159. Associated study: Scientific Reports (2023), doi:10.1038/s41598-023-45466-9.

selection.name: Cochlea fluid space
selection.evidence: Original manually labeled Dataset A CT fluid-space class, retained in the paired source grid; no project subdivision or geometric refinement.
notes: Original Dataset A cadaveric specimen 1; separate from clinical Dataset B.
The label describes the inner-ear fluid-space annotation, not a separately segmented nerve, sensory epithelium or membranous labyrinth.
The source file does not explicitly declare specimen laterality; coordinate offset is not used to infer a side.
Reconstructed sampling is about 0.0986 mm; the publication reports acquired slice thickness of 0.466 mm. Sampling is not a claim of isotropic acquired resolution.
The three separately supplied landmark records have unresolved IJK-to-LPS residuals and are not integrated as verified teaching targets.

source_case.cohort: Dataset A: 43 cadaveric temporal bones; clinical Dataset B excluded
source_case.landmarks: Preserved in original HDF5; not integrated because original IJK and XYZ records do not agree within half a voxel diagonal.

license_downloads.evidence: Publisher declaration of CC BY 4.0 for the fixed source record. The local snapshot is retained unchanged and its exact hash becomes part of the package identity.

acquisition: Install the hdf5 optional dependency in the NeuroImage environment, then run neuroimage acquire inner_ear_ct_specimen1 --data-root <data-root>. Only the selected Dataset A specimen and publisher license declaration are required.

teaching_sequences.title: The three source-defined inner-ear spaces
teaching_sequences.objective: Locate the cochlear, vestibular and canal fluid-space labels in the original cadaveric CT and compare their spatial relationships.
teaching_sequences.instruction: Follow each source label in axial, coronal and sagittal sections. Reduce overlay opacity to inspect the corresponding original CT. Rotate the complete three-structure surface set, then return to full sections.
teaching_sequences.evidence_limit: One source specimen with three fluid-space classes. Membranous subdivisions, individual canal names and cochlear turns are not separately labeled; the source does not establish specimen laterality.

steps.prompt: Follow the cochlear fluid-space label through adjacent CT sections and compare its coiled source surface with the vestibular label.
steps.question: Which findings come from the CT and which come from the source annotation?

steps.prompt: Keep all three structures visible and follow the vestibular label between the cochlear and canal fluid-space assignments.
steps.question: How does this source define the vestibular class, and which neighboring classes can you select independently?

steps.prompt: Rotate the combined canal label, then check its source extent on the CT. The source groups all canal fluid spaces in one value.
steps.question: Does the source provide separately selectable anterior, posterior and lateral canals?

teaching_sequences.title: Sampling, boundaries and original source coordinates
teaching_sequences.objective: Distinguish source sampling, CT intensity values and computed label surfaces from independently verified fine anatomical boundaries.
teaching_sequences.instruction: Compare the CT with overlay opacity at zero and at a low value. Magnify at the same native target and inspect neighboring sections. The unsmoothed 0.5 isosurface is a display of the categorical voxel boundary.
teaching_sequences.evidence_limit: The 98.6 micrometer reconstruction grid does not establish equal acquired resolution. Original CT integers lack embedded calibration metadata; independent landmark discrepancies remain excluded from teaching targets.
teaching_sequences.step_prompt: Compare the original CT texture, source label overlay and derived surface at the same native voxel target.
teaching_sequences.step_question: Which observation is supported by the original image, which by manual labeling, and which by display interpolation?
